note: Names, providers and dates only. Never a value, a secret id or a Bitwarden item id.

credentials.label: cron-job.org GitHub token
credentials.used_for: starts the hourly pipeline from cron-job.org (backup to the Oracle ticker)
credentials.how_read: date recorded by hand when the token was made; GitHub returns a fine-grained token's expiry in the github-authentication-token-expiration header of any API answer; not read yet, so enter the date by hand until it is
credentials.renew: renew the fine-grained token in GitHub settings, paste it into the cron-job.org job

credentials.label: Outlook sign-in token
credentials.used_for: reads the Outlook calendar and mail (a personal and a work mailbox)
credentials.read_in: workflows calendar.yml, outlook.yml, domains.yml (OUTLOOK_CLIENT_ID); lifeos/outlook. Bitwarden secret names: project OPENCLAW: openclaw/outlook/clientId; project OUTLOOK: openclaw/outlook/personal/mailboxFingerprint, openclaw/outlook/personal/refreshToken, openclaw/outlook/work/mailboxFingerprint, openclaw/outlook/work/refreshToken
credentials.how_read: Microsoft refresh tokens roll over each time they are used and Microsoft gives LIFE OS no expiry date for them; the client id and the mailbox fingerprints are identifiers, not credentials that expire. Nothing here can warn, so it shows No expiry exposed
credentials.renew: if the Outlook sign-in stops working, sign in again for that mailbox and store the new refresh token in Bitwarden under the same name
